holidays.name: Pandemonium Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace chaos. Toss out the schedule, say yes to the unexpected, and find the fun in life's messiness. It's also a nudge to pause and bring a little balance back afterward.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. The word 'pandemonium' comes from the Greek 'pan' (all) and the Latin 'daemonium' (evil spirit).
holidays.funFact: John Milton coined 'pandemonium' in Paradise Lost (1667). He used it as the name of the capital of Hell, the palace of all demons.

holidays.name: National Mac and Cheese Day
holidays.description: A salute to the ultimate comfort food, from the blue-box classic to fancy baked versions with a crackly breadcrumb crust. Cook up a pot and don't skimp on the cheese.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that has been observed on July 14 for years. It celebrates the dish's long reign as a cozy staple.
holidays.funFact: Thomas Jefferson is often credited with popularizing macaroni and cheese in America after he served a pasta-and-cheese dish at an 1802 state dinner.

holidays.name: National Grand Marnier Day
holidays.description: A toast to the French liqueur that blends Cognac with bitter orange essence. Sip it neat, splash it in a Cosmopolitan, or drizzle it over crêpes for a boozy treat.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food and drink observance that honors the orange liqueur first created in France in 1880. It conveniently lands on Bastille Day, which is French too.
holidays.funFact: Grand Marnier was created by Louis-Alexandre Marnier Lapostolle. Cesar Ritz is said to have suggested the name.
